dataIdInfo.idPurp: The Reneco Management Areas are the collection of the areas spanning from northern Africa to Eastern Asia where Reneco targets its actions for various founders.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
The Reneco Management Areas are built on three nested type of entity: the “working area”, the “working region”, and the “management unit” with the following definitions:

  • LEVEL 1 - “Working area”: a zone allocated to a Reneco founders and Reneco would be involved in the management ora zone not allocated to any Reneco founders but where Reneco would work or lead surveys

  • LEVEL 2 – “Working region” is a subdivision of the “working area”, defined by fieldwork activities.

  • LEVEL 3 – “Management unit” is a subdivision of “working region” with a bivalent status based on Houbara hunting activity or Houbara Protection (the status can also be unknown).

Also, a “working area” can be defined as “special” if the area is a zone not under specific agreement and where Reneco can operate upon request. In that special case, the two lower levels of the “working area special” are the “working region special” and the “management unit special”.

The Reneco Management Areas feature class is stored in geographic coordinate system WGS 1984 (EPSG: 4326). Each record has the geometry of a single-polygon or a multi-polygon and represents the boundary of either a “working area”, a “working region” or a “management unit”.

The Reneco Management Areas respects the following topology rules:

  • A “working area” is completely within the boundary of a country.

  • A “working area” is not overlapping any other “working area”.

  • A “working area” is completely divided in one or more “working regions”.

  • A “working region” is completely within a “working area”.

  • A “working region” is not overlapping any other “working region”.

  • A “working region” is completely divided in one or more “management unit”.

  • A “management unit” is completely within a “working region”.

  • A “management unit” is not overlapping any other “management unit”.
